clue.text: Ibsen's model residence

parts.note: a toy home for dolls is a model residence, and Ibsen's best-known play takes that title

explanation.walkthrough: A doll's house is a miniature model of a home, and Henrik Ibsen's 1879 play bears that exact name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist's famous play is named after a child's miniature toy home.

clue.text: Drugs obtained from sap

explanation.surface: Narcotics extracted from plant juices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' looks like plant juice, the source of the drug; it is the second definition, a gullible fool.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a dope is both a narcotic and a stupid person, the same as a sap.

clue.text: Arranged substantial rise for a Shakespearean player

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the pieces from the bottom upwards, so the whole run is turned backwards

parts.note: arranged means set, as a table is set
substantial means real, having solid existence

explanation.surface: An actor in a Shakespeare play is cast after a big increase in the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns SETREAL into LAERTES. 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal but gives SET.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a character in Hamlet, Ophelia's brother, so a role played on stage in Shakespeare.

clue.text: A market for blended ales

indicators.note: blended means the letters of the word ales are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A place to buy mixed beers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is an event where goods are offered for purchase, a kind of market.

clue.text: A winger, taking loot, ran off

indicators.note: off means the letters of loot and ran have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief grabbed the booty and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a bird. 'ran off' reads as fleeing; 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, a bird, and birds fly on wings.

clue.text: A come-down — no two ways about that!

indicators.note: about means the two compass letters go around the other piece

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction or way
W is west, a second compass direction
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drop in fortune, and there is no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no two ways about that' reads as 'undeniably'; really NO sits inside S and W, two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of it fall from the sky in winter, so it literally comes down.

clue.text: Used by the Gallic instructor on board?

definitions.text: Used by the Gallic instructor on board?

parts.words: Used by the Gallic instructor on board?
parts.note: a teacher from France writing on a blackboard would use the white stick of his own nationality

explanation.walkthrough: This is really a soft talc used by tailors to mark cloth; the clue pretends it is a French teacher's blackboard stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailor's talc shares its name with what a teacher from Gaul might write with on a blackboard.

clue.text: Pilot a plane quite new in style

indicators.note: quite new means the letters of pilot a plane are made into something entirely fresh

explanation.surface: Flying an aircraft in a completely novel manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is a noun meaning a title or name, not a manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to name them, and a name or title is an appellation.

clue.text: Looks for fruit among the assorted canapés

indicators.note: among means one piece is placed amid the letters of the other
assorted means the letters of canapés are mixed up

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Searching for fruit within a mixed plate of party snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts PEAR inside APANCES, the anagram of CANAPES signalled by 'assorted'. 'Looks' seems a verb; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's looks are their outward aspect, how they seem to others.

clue.text: Patriot presenting people with a catalogue

parts.note: a people is a nation
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A loyal citizen offers a country along with an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: One devoted to their country's independence or interests is a patriot.

clue.text: He aims to put his clients on a good footing!

definitions.text: He aims to put his clients on a good footing!

parts.words: He aims to put his clients on a good footing!
parts.note: a good footing usually means a sound basis; here it means healthy feet

explanation.walkthrough: 'on a good footing' sounds like business advice, but it means literally helping customers' feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot specialist treats patients' feet, literally improving their footing.

clue.text: Mature, so given rent and key

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Grown-up enough to have paid rent and been given a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for housing; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or ideas that are fully developed are ready, grown-up.

clue.text: Clean area of the English coast

definitions.meaning: The ..., a square bay on England's east coast between Lincolnshire and Norfolk

explanation.surface: A tidy stretch of English shoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a large shallow bay on England's east coast where Lincolnshire meets Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to make clean, and the Wash is a named bay on the eastern coastline.

clue.text: Sewers that are almost totally superfluous

indicators.note: almost totally means the word is used nearly complete, with only its last letter dropped

parts.note: superfluous means needless, unnecessary

explanation.surface: Drains that are pretty much entirely unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' suggests drains; it means things that sew. 'almost totally' drops the final S of NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that sew stitches are sewing tools with an eye for thread.

clue.text: A woman's jocular retort

definitions.meaning: a woman's name, the 's being 'is' joining the two definitions

explanation.surface: A lady makes a funny comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name and also a witty sortie or quip in reply.

clue.text: The breeder's not so simple!

definitions.meaning: one who breeds animals such as pigeons, the 's being 'is'
more elaborate, the comparative of an adjective meaning ornate

explanation.surface: A breeder of animals is more complicated than he seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon or dog breeder is called a fancier, and fancy is the opposite of plain, so fancier is less plain.

clue.text: Establish there's nothing in reserve

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a reserve of money is a fund
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Determine that the savings are empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an organisation is to set it up, institute it.

clue.text: Boy getting round a cross old German

indicators.note: getting round means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: a son is a boy
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A lad gets around an angry elderly German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective, angry, but gives the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxons were an ancient Germanic people who settled in England.

clue.text: Hot time for one of the immortals

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A heated period for a god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was queen of the gods, wife of Zeus, and deities never die.

clue.text: Photograph game

definitions.meaning: a children's card game where matching cards are called

explanation.surface: A picture of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a casual picture, and the card game is won by calling out on matching pairs.

clue.text: Drink being left, make a song about it

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to make a song is to sing

explanation.surface: A drink is abandoned, so someone complains loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a song about it' reads as 'complain'; really SING goes about L.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water.

clue.text: Pilot holding up many a ship

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: to pilot is to steer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

explanation.surface: A pilot delays many vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MA into AM, which goes inside STEER. 'holding up' looks like delaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam power is a ship.

clue.text: Military leader putting points in large assembly

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A commander makes points at a big meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' looks like a meeting; it is the anagram signal for EN plus LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking army officer commanding troops is a general.

clue.text: Growing integrity

definitions.meaning: describes a plant, something that grows in a garden

explanation.surface: Increasing moral uprightness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing' stands for a plant: honesty is a garden flower with silvery seed pods.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a garden flower with papery discs and the virtue of being truthful.

clue.text: Dirty, over-fed, idle, affected

indicators.note: affected means the letters of fed and idle are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Grubby, overeating, lazy and pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like one more adjective in the list but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soiled or made unclean has been polluted, sullied.

clue.text: Offering cash, always look sly

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, a sum of money
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone always offers money with a crafty look.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to cast a lascivious or knowing sideways glance.

clue.text: A floating mass of logs is right behind

parts.note: aft means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Logs drifting on a river sit to the right and behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashed timbers drifting on water form a crude platform or boat.

clue.text: How the woolly-minded make use of 13

definitions.text: How the woolly-minded make use of 13

parts.words: How the woolly-minded make use of 13
parts.note: 13 across names tools for sewing; people with wool on their minds use them to make garments

explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly-minded' usually means muddled; here it means people keen on wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Working yarn with a pair of sewing tools creates a woolly garment.

clue.text: Crawlers getting a fool to accept small change

indicators.note: to accept means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: an ass is a fool
P stands for penny, small change

explanation.surface: Creeps get a fool to take a few coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawlers' suggests flatterers; it means snakes, which crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Small venomous snakes slither along the ground.

clue.text: Some chateau delightfully situated in France

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A castle in a lovely French setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Aude is a department and river in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a region of southern France, so a place located there.

clue.text: Fish and stout — normal combination

indicators.note: combination means the letters of stout and normal are combined and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish and dark beer make a standard pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea trout are a migratory fish with pink flesh, also called by this name.

clue.text: The spinner of tales unlikely to be given credit?

definitions.meaning: one who spins yarns or narrates
someone telling stories is not to be believed, and a bank teller grants no credit

explanation.surface: A yarn-spinner can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is cryptic: a fibber is not believed, or credited.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator of yarns, also a fibber whose words are not believed.
